blockers.summary: Docker Desktop cannot start. CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (session 13): this is NOT a stale socket from an unclean shutdown. The run directory was renamed aside; Docker recreated it, created a brand-new sailor-ingest.sock, and failed on that newly-created file with the same "file cannot be accessed by the system" error (timestamp confirmed six minutes old). A second socket dir (docker-secrets-engine) failed identically. This machine cannot create usable AF_UNIX socket reparse points, which points at an antivirus/EDR filesystem filter driver or a damaged Windows AF_UNIX subsystem.
blockers.impact: No live Postgres/Redis/Qdrant. Migration 0009 (per-person attribution) has never been applied to a real database, and the three DB-level tests added in session 13 skip rather than run. They do execute in CI, which provisions Postgres.
blockers.workaround: Not fixable from a shell. Options, in order of likely success: Docker Desktop -> Troubleshoot -> Reset to factory defaults; exclude %LOCALAPPDATA%Docker from real-time AV scanning; reinstall Docker Desktop. A plain machine restart may not be sufficient since the sockets are broken at creation, not stale. Leftover inert dirs to delete once working: %LOCALAPPDATA%Dockerun.stale and %LOCALAPPDATA%docker-secrets-engine.stale.

fixed_session_7.summary: cache/semantic.rs was fully built since session 1 and never called from the live pipeline (flagged by session 3's and session 5's audits, deliberately deferred as a product decision). Wired into routes/openai_compat.rs::execute_with_headroom behind a new cache::embed::Embedder trait (embedding on Aegis's own pooled provider credential, never a customer's BYOK key), gated to Pro/Enterprise plans. A semantic hit also promotes its own wording into the exact-match tier.

New, beyond the original audit scope -- the founder asked directly for a way to keep cost savings from caching without keeping content around indefinitely. Added cache::durable::DurableCache: a fingerprint the hot Redis tier has already proven repeats gets promoted to an encrypted Postgres row (AES-256-GCM, per-tenant HKDF key, same shape as provider_credentials), sliding 30-day TTL, purged on the existing 04:00 UTC scheduler window. See docs/adr/0008-tiered-durable-cache.md.

cache::semantic::QdrantVectorStore talked REST/JSON only, deliberately deferred when first raised (founder chose 'embedding fix only, for now'). Picked back up once the embedding fix (ort) made Qdrant's own round trip a proportionally bigger slice of the remaining latency. Added cache::qdrant_grpc::QdrantGrpcVectorStore, a second VectorStore impl chosen via a new QDRANT_GRPC_URL config setting (REST kept as the fallback when unset). Unlike ort, qdrant-client is pure Rust with no native-binary problem, so this is FULLY verified at the type/link/test level -- cargo check, cargo clippy --all-targets, and the full cargo test suite all pass with this dependency compiled in by default. Not verified: behavior against a live Qdrant server (no Docker here). Caught and fixed a real cargo-audit regression along the way (tokenizers -> paste, RUSTSEC-2024-0436, scoped ignore added to .cargo/audit.toml) and a documentation inaccuracy (the ADR draft claimed the bundled self-hosted Qdrant already exposed gRPC on 6334; it didn't -- added the port mapping to both docker-compose files instead of leaving the doc wrong). See docs/adr/0010-qdrant-grpc-client.md.

Budget checking bounded aggregate spend over a period; nothing bounded a single request's max_tokens independent of that -- a prompt with no max_tokens (or an agent loop requesting far more than the budget projection assumed) could land as a large, surprising outlier before the aggregate counter caught up. Added Config::max_tokens_per_request (AEGIS_MAX_TOKENS_PER_REQUEST, default 16384) enforced by a shared clamp_max_tokens(), called from both HTTP entry points (handle_chat, handle_messages) before their budget reservation -- covers streaming and non-streaming from one call site per endpoint (a naive implementation inside execute_with_headroom alone would have missed streaming entirely, since stream_chat runs a separate pipeline; caught this before shipping and moved the enforcement point). Also fixes budget-projection accuracy: the reservation now projects against the bound that will actually be enforced. Fully verified: extended MockProvider::RecordedCall to capture the max_tokens a provider actually received, proved the streaming case specifically with a dedicated test. 8 new tests, all passing.

experimental_unverified.summary: cache::onnx_embed::OnnxEmbedder (ort + tokenizers, target model BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, FP32, mean-pooled + L2-normalized), a second Embedder implementation for a local, sub-2ms-target embedding path replacing ProviderEmbedder's 50-300ms remote call. Model chosen after comparing against the originally-proposed all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and against NVIDIA's open embedding line (Nemotron 3 Embed) -- NVIDIA ruled out on size/architecture fit (smallest variant 1.14B params, GPU-quantized), not license (OpenMDW-1.1 is actually commercial-friendly). Behind an off-by-default 'local-embeddings' Cargo feature specifically so it never affects the default build.
experimental_unverified.verified: cargo check --features local-embeddings succeeds (type-checks against the real ort v2.0.0-rc.10 / tokenizers v0.23 APIs, one real borrow-checker bug caught and fixed). cargo clippy --features local-embeddings --lib is clean. Default (no-flag) cargo build/test confirmed unaffected before and after -- still 774 lib / 814 full-suite.
experimental_unverified.not_verified: cargo build/cargo test WITH the feature fail to link -- confirmed directly (ort-sys emits a self-explanatory placeholder linker input when no ONNX Runtime binary is configured). This means even the pure mean-pooling/normalization unit tests, which need no model at all, have never actually run -- only been reviewed by hand. No real ONNX Runtime binary or bge-small-en-v1.5 model file exists in this environment, and this crate deliberately does not fetch either automatically. Also unverified: the false-positive rate of the 0.95 similarity threshold specifically for this model's embedding space -- BGE's own docs note its unrelated-text similarity baseline sits well above zero, so this is a real open question, not a formality.
